text.p: McDonald's Corp, which is reorganizing its U.S. business into five geographic divisions, said Wednesday it named several U.S. executives to new positions.

The fast-food giant named Claire Babrowski as senior vice president of restaurant systems, a newly created position that includes U.S. site development, purchasing, operations research and development, menu management and training.
McDonald's also named Patrick Flynn as executive vice president of strategic planning and Raymond Mines as senior vice president of franchisee relations.
It said Flynn brings more than 35 years of experience to this new function, which will include business planning and research, corporate development and new technology.

"In another critical area, franchisee relations, Raymond Mines will work with our division presidents to maintain a sharp focus on the needs and concerns of our owner/operators," Jack Greenberg, chairman of the McDonald's USA unit, said in a statement. "When it is all said and done, McDonald's cannot succeed unless our franchisees succeed."
Some McDonald's franchisees have been critical of the company, which has more than 21,000 restaurants worldwide and over 12,000 in the United States.

Some franchisees have said the chain's rapid expansion has hurt store profitability. They were also critical of a national price promotion known as Campaign 55, saying it did not drive sales and hurt profit margins.
In May, the company discontinued most of Campaign 55, which had offered featured hamburgers for 55 cents when customers also bought french fries and a drink.
Also on Wednesday, McDonald's named Noel Kaplan to the newly created position of senior vice president for alliance relationships, to enhance McDonald's global strategic alliances.
It was not immediately known what positions Babrowski, Flynn, Mines and Kaplan had held at McDonald's.
